title: Analyzing the Safety of Japanese Large Language Models in Stereotype-Triggering Prompts

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing age-related group terms (e.g., child, high school student), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing disability-related group terms (e.g., blind person), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing gender-related group terms (e.g., female, male), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing physical appearance-related group terms (e.g., short person, thin person), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing sexual orientation-related group terms (e.g., bisexual person), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing nationality-related group terms (e.g., Japanese, Chinese), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing profession-related group terms (e.g., accountant, doctor), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing region-related group terms (e.g., people from Hokkaido), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.

Analyzing open-ended LLM responses to stereotype-triggering prompts containing religion-related group terms (e.g., Buddhist, catholic), and measuring refusal rates, toxicity via Perspective API, and sentiment using a BERT-based classifier.
